sentences.text: 1 This is a claim petition filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .15,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 19.05.2024 at about 03.45 p.m., he, along with his wife and children, was travelling on a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-08-Q-4133 from Mudaram Doddi to their village and while passing near Bangla Vuru Village, V.Kota Mandalam on V.Kota-Pernumbat NH Road, Chittor District, Andhra Pradesh, a Hyundai Eon Car bearing Regn.No.TN-18-AH-5595, driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the motor cycle.

Due to the accident, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter shifted to Government Hospital V.Kota and then referred to PES Hospital, Kuppam,
wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical,
conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.

Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was Supervisor at Rainbow Interiors,
JP Nagar, Bengaluru and was getting salary of Rs.44,800/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of Car by its driver.
The respondent, being the owner, is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. The respondent not engaged the services of counsel in spite of granting sufficient opportunities and hence, respondent is considered to be contesting the petitioner in her individual capacity.
Respondent not filed the written statement in spite of according opportunities and as such, written statement of respondent is treated nil.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:
POINTS 1.

Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 19.05.2024 at about 03.45 p.m., near at Bangla vuru village, V.Kota Mandalam, on V.Kota- Pernumbat Road, Chittor District, AP, when petitioner was riding his Motor Cycle bearing Regn.NO.KA-08-Q-4133 along with family members, due to the rash and negligent driving of Hyundai Eon Car bearing Regn.No.TN-18-AH-5595 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?

3 . What order or award?
5.

In order to prove the contention of the petition, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1, got examined Medical Record Officer at PES Hospital Kuppam, Chittoor District, A.P. as PW.2, and Dr.B.Ramesh, who is working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18 and closed evidence of his side.

The respondent not Anand Kumar T S vs Suriyaprabha K on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142348712/
2 adduced evidence on her behalf.

sentences.text: 6. Heard the argument of counsel for petitioner.
Argument of respondent is treated nil.
Perused the materials available on record.

7. Findings of this tribunal on the above points are under:-
Point No.1: In the Affirmative;
Point No.2: Partly in the Affirmative; Point No.3: As per final order for the following:-

8. Point No.1:- The petitioner contended that on 19.05.2024 at about 03.45 p.m., accident occurred near at Bangla vuru village, V.Kota-Pernumbat Road, Chittor District, AP, when petitioner was riding his Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-08-Q-4133, due to the rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.TN-18-AH-5595 by its driver in which he sustained grievous injuries.
9.
Further, in order to prove accident, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.2 and P.2(a), first information statement and its translated version.

On perusal of Ex.P.2 and P.2(a), first information statement, one of relatives of petitioner by name Sri.D.M.Venkataramana S/o Late Muneppa has lodged complaint with police on 20.05.2024 pertaining to the accident occurred on 19.05.2024.
The police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.337 of IPC.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
Ex.P.1 discloses the aspect of registration of FIR against the driver of offending car.
The petitioner also furnished copy of spot mahazar and spot sketch and its translated version, which are marked as Ex.P.3 and P.5 and P.3(a) and P.5(a).
The said documents disclose that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said documents.
In the mahazar also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The respondent not placed any satisfactory materials in order to show that the place of accident, as described in the mahazar and sketch, are contrary to the actual facts.
The sketch discloses the aspect of occurrence of accident in the route in which the petitioner has been travelling.
The sketch furnished by petitioner discloses that the offending vehicle came to right side in which the petitioner is going.
The sketch furnished by petitioner also discloses the aspect of negligence on the part of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
Ex.P.4 is the Wound certificate which discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner in the road traffic accident.
The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.337 & 338 and Sec.146 R/w.196 of M.V.Act as per Ex.P.7.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The respondent, being owner of offending vehicle, does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.

No satisfactory materials are placed by the Anand Kumar T S vs Suriyaprabha K on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142348712/
3 respondent to show that the investigation is not conducted in proper manner.

sentences.text: The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondent not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.

10. The petitioner got examined as PW.1 and filed the affidavit in lieu of chief examination wherein he stated the aspect of occurrence of accident due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The respondent, though appeared before the Tribunal, not cross examined PW.1 in order to rebut or controvert the contention of petitioner.
The evidence of PW.1 remains unrebutted and unchallenged.

11. No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioner pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
12. The respondent not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondent not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of record, it discloses that accident was caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.7, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.TN-18-AH-5595 by its driver and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Point No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
13. Point No.2:
The petitioner succeeded in establishing that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of driver of car vehicle.
As Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

The Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc., in order to assess the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled.
i) Towards injury, pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident she sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.

In order to prove the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner produced Wound certificate issued by PES Institute of Medical Sciences &
Research marked at Ex.P.4.

sentences.text: The said document discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner and that the injuries are grievous in nature.

The petitioner also produced Ex.P.6, Discharge Summary which discloses the aspect of availing Anand Kumar T S vs Suriyaprabha K on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142348712/
4 treatment by petitioner for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

Further, the petitioner examined Dr.B.Ramesh as PW.3 and got marked Ex.P17 & 18 documents.
PW.3/doctor deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of permanent physical disability and assessed the disability to the right lower limb at 30% and to whole body at 15%.

On consideration of the materials placed before the Tribunal,
compensation of .50,000/- appears just and reasonable towards Pain and Suffering.
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses:- The petitioner has not produced any medical bills to show that he has taken treatment in the hospital.
The petitioner not furnished any materials in order to show the expenses incurred by him for the treatment of injuries.
No materials are placed by the petitioner to show the aspect of expenses incurred by him towards treatment.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the petitioner cannot be considered to be entitled to compensation towards medical expenses.
As such petitioner is not entitled for compensation towards medical expenses.
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges:- On perusal of records, the accident occurred on 19.05.2024 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient at the hospital.

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.6, Discharge Summary issued by PES Institute of Medical Sciences and Research, which discloses the aspect of availing treatment by petitioner as an inpatient from 19.05.2024 to 04.06.2024 i.e., for a period of 17 days.

sentences.text: On perusal of materials on record, the petitioner appears to have admitted as an inpatient at Hospital pertaining to the injuries sustained by him and availed treatment as an inpatient.
The petitioner might have required good food during the period of treatment.

Considering the said facts, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .500/- per day for 17 days to a sum of .8,500/- appears just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant.
(iv) Towards Conveyance:-

The petitioner is the resident of Gummireddipalli Village, V.Kota Mandalam,
Palamaner Taluk, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh and he has admitted to hospital for treatment.
In order to prove this aspect the petitioner has produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P.6.
The petitioner might have incurred expenses for conveyance during the period of treatment.
Considering the injuries sustained and facts of the case, the tribunal is of view that the compensation of .10,000/- appears just and proper towards conveyance charges.

(v) Towards loss of income during treatment:-
The petitioner contended that he was Supervisor at Rainbow Interiors, JP Nagar,
Bengaluru and getting salary for a sum of .44,800/- per month.
In order to prove the income, the petitioner not produced any documents.
The petitioner not furnished any materials to show that he was earning .44,800/- per month.

In order to substantiate the said contention, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.11 - Letter issued Anand Kumar T S vs Suriyaprabha K on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142348712/
5 by Rainbow Interiors, wherein it is mentioned that Sri.T.S.Anand Kumar was working in their company Rain Bow Interior as a Supervisor.

sentences.text: In order to substantiate the same, the petitioner has not examined the author of the said document.
The petitioner not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to substantiate his contention regarding occupation and income.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, notional is to be taken into consideration.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the notional income of the petitioner considered as .16,500/-.
On perusal of record, it appears that petitioner might have not attended his work for some time due to accidental injuries.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for .30,000/- towards loss of income during treatment.

(vi) Towards Loss of future earning capacity:-
The petitioner has contended that due to accident, he was admitted as an inpatient at Hospital and sustained permanent disablement.
The petitioner also examined Dr.B.Ramesh working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru as PW.3.
PW.3/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess disabilities.
The doctor deposed that petitioner has sustained injuries like fracture of both bone right leg with soft tissue injury and underwent internal fixation of tibia and later discharged.
Further petitioner complains of pain in right leg difficulty to squat on floor, sit cross legged climb upstairs walk on slope kneel stand on affected limb and difficult to do routine activities.
Further PW.3 deposed that as per radiological examination shows fracture united with implant in situ.
The doctor has assessed the disability to the right lower limb at 30% and to the whole body at 15%.
In order to prove the disability, the doctor has produced OPD book and X-ray marked at Ex.P.17 & 18.
PW.3 not stated that the petitioner could not be able to do his routine activities in a normal way.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the petitioner to show that the petitioner is unable to do any work at all.
The injuries sustained by petitioner do not appear to cause much problem in doing his activities.

The petitioner also examined Medical Record Officer at PES Hospital, Kuppam, Chittoor District, AP as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.12 to 16 i.e., authorization letter, MLC Register extract, police intimation, case sheet and X-ray films.
By considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do his work with difficulty.
As per ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another and considering facts and circumstances of the case, the functional disability is assessed at 07%.

The accident occurred on 19.05.2024.

sentences.text: In the absence of materials to the contrary, the document furnished by petitioner is to be considered for ascertaining the age of petitioner.
As per the document placed before the Tribunal, the age of petitioner was 40 years at the time of accident and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier.
As per Smt.Sarla Verma case multiplier applicable is '15'.
As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay Kumar and another, this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of his gross income.

sentences.text:
Hence, future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under :
Annual Income before accident : (.16,500/- x 12) = .1,98,000/-
Loss of future earning p.a. (07% of prior annual income) = .13,860/-.
Multiplier applicable with reference to age - 15 Loss of future earnings - (.13,860/- x 15) = .2,07,900/-.
The petitioner is entitled for .2,07,900/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
(vii) Deprivation of Future Amenities:-
The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he is unable to do his day- today activities as earlier.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .10,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future amenities.

(viii) Towards Future Medical Expenses:
The doctor/PW.3 has opined that the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implant.
No materials are placed before the Tribunal to ascertain the aspect of expenses required for future surgery for removal of implants.
The petitioner not furnished any materials related to cost of future surgery.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case .20,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future medical expenses.

15. In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

sentences.text: 16. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondent.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.TN-18-AH-5595 by its driver.
The materials on record disclose that the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective policy of insurance at the time of accident.
In the absence of valid insurance policy, the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation.
So, the respondent, being the owner of the offending vehicle, is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Point No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
17. Point No.3:-

In view of the findings given on the above said points, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .3,36,400/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Thirty Six Thousand Four Hundred only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
(future medical expenses shall not carry any interest)
Respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
Entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of petitioner as amount is meager one.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .3,36,400/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Thirty Six Thousand Four Hundred only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
(future medical expenses shall not carry any interest)
Respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
Entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of petitioner as amount is meager one.
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.
The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
The Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
